newsitem.title: USA: Minn House committee approves $1.58 bln tax relief.
newsitem.headline: Minn House committee approves $1.58 bln tax relief.

text.p: A Minnesota House committee on Thursday approved a three-year $1.58 billion tax relief package that goes hand-in-hand with increasing state funding to schools, a fiscal analyst for the House said.

The House ways and means committee approved the planned spending on a voice vote, sending the 416-page omnibus bill to the full House for consideration on Friday, said Matt Shands, a fiscal analyst for the tax committee.
The bill calls for more than $1.39 billion in local property tax relief over the next three years, including a $200 million property tax rebate for property owners and renters in 1997, Shands said.
That rebate amounts to an 8.5 percent cut for the current year, which can be received next year, Shands said.
Another $188 million of relief was approved for other areas, Shands added.
The bill also would impose tax caps, but makes exceptions for local governments that must deal with flood damages, debt service or state welfare reform mandates, Shands said.
The state share of funding for elementary and secondary schools would increase from 60 percent to 70 percent of the total costs as well, Shands said.
The relief would be funded in part through Minnesota's projected $2.3 billion budget surplus, generated through large increases in sales and income tax revenues.
Critics of the tax relief package have questioned whether the budget surplus is sustainable or the cuts now will be a one-shot deal.
Economists for the state suggest, however, that the surplus is a result of sustainable growth rather than "a blip" on among economic indicators, Shands said.
Minnesota operates on a two-year budget. The next fiscal biennium begins on July 1.
